result:
The change is complete and verified: `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` is 5/5 green (including three new registration tests), and `bunx guren check` reports no new warnings.

**What I changed**

Registration now hands the welcome email to the queue instead of sending it inline. `RegisterController.store()` (`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts:31`) dispatches `SendWelcomeEmailJob` with the registered name and address after the account is created and the session established, then redirects to `/dashboard` exactly as before — a refused registration (validation error or taken email) throws before the dispatch, so nothing is queued or sent. `app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts` resolves the mailer at run time (so a worker in another process works the same) and sends `app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts`, a mailable whose subject is `Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!` with a plain-text greeting; the sender comes from the manager's configured `from`. Neither subsystem existed yet, so I brought both up the way this project structures configuration: `config/queue.ts` and `config/mail.ts` build the managers from `QUEUE_CONNECTION` (`sync` / `memory` / `redis`) and `MAIL_MAILER` (`log` / `memory` / `resend`, sender from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`), with `app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts` and `app/Providers/MailProvider.ts` binding them into the container, installing them where queued work reads them, and registering the job class so a wire name resolves back to a class; both are registered in `src/app.ts`, which also publishes the app container for jobs running outside a request. `config/app.ts` gained an `appName()` helper, `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` covers queue-not-send, worker-delivers-one-message, and refused-registration-queues-nothing, and `docs/adr/0002-queue-the-welcome-email-after-registration.md` records the decision.
